criteria_results.evidence: build_nats_client() reads GUARDKIT_NATS_PASSWORD from environment or optional env_file parameter. Raises ValueError with actionable message 'GUARDKIT_NATS_PASSWORD is not set or is blank. Set this environment variable to the provisioned guardkit user password...' if missing or blank. Tests TestBuildNatsClient::test_missing_password_raises_actionable_error and test_blank_password_raises_actionable_error verify error handling with specific message patterns.

build_nats_client() constructs NATSConfig at line 79 with exact parameters: url='nats://127.0.0.1:4222', user='guardkit', password=SecretStr(password), name='guardkit-harvest'. Then passes config to NATSClient at line 87 with source_id='guardkit-harvest'. Tests TestBuildNatsClient::test_builds_config_with_correct_parameters and test_builds_client_with_correct_source_id verify construction parameters via mock assertions.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Publish lifecycle: `await client.connect()` → for each episode
criteria_results.evidence: publish_episodes() implements exact lifecycle at lines 119-148: await client.connect() (line 119), for loop with await client.publish_episode(episode) per episode (line 124), finally block with await client.disconnect() (line 148). Uses .disconnect() method as specified, not .close(). Test TestPublishEpisodes::test_publish_lifecycle_ordering verifies call sequence with mock.assert_has_calls() checking connect → publish × N → disconnect ordering.

criteria_results.criterion_text: A `publish_episode` `ValueError` (body > 900 KB) is caught **per episode**: that
criteria_results.evidence: ValueError from publish_episode is caught in per-episode try/except block at lines 133-144. Skipped episodes increment result.skipped_oversized (line 136) and log warning at lines 138-144 with format 'Skipped oversized episode {episode_id} ({size_bytes} bytes, >{MAX_EPISODE_BODY_BYTES} byte limit). chunk upstream'. Loop continues after skip (exception caught, not re-raised). Tests TestPublishEpisodes::test_oversized_episode_skipped_with_actionable_message and test_oversized_episode_does_not_abort_run verify handling: skipped count increments, actionable logging, and run continues to publish remaining episodes after an oversized one.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Idempotent / resumable: no client-side dedupe state; correctness relies on the
criteria_results.evidence: No client-side deduplication state exists in publish_episodes() or PublishResult. Implementation publishes all episodes every run with no skip/cache logic (lines 122-131 publish every episode in sequence). JetStream deduplication via Nats-Msg-Id header is handled by NATSClient.publish_episode() (delegated, not implemented here per AC-006). Test TestPublishEpisodes::test_idempotent_deterministic_episode_ids verifies re-running with same episodes calls publish_episode with identical episode_ids in same order.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Does **not** hand-roll NATS publishing, subject construction, or the
criteria_results.evidence: Implementation delegates all NATS operations to NATSClient.publish_episode() at line 124. No direct NATS protocol code, subject string construction, header setting, or nats.js imports. Only calls client.connect(), client.publish_episode(episode), client.disconnect(). All NATS publishing details (subject resolution, Nats-Msg-Id header, JetStream publish) handled by nats_core library methods. Verified by code review of harvest_publisher.py - no NATS wire protocol or subject formatting logic present.

publish_episodes() returns PublishResult dataclass (defined lines 25-37) with published: int (line 35), skipped_oversized: int (line 36), counts_per_type: dict[str, int] (line 37). Result populated during publish loop: published increments at line 125, skipped_oversized increments at line 136, counts_per_type tracks episodes per episode_type at lines 128-131. Test TestPublishEpisodes::test_returns_publish_summary verifies return type is PublishResult and all three fields are populated correctly after publishing.

criteria_results.criterion_text: Unit tests use a **fake/mock `NATSClient`** (no live broker) asserting:
criteria_results.evidence: All tests use AsyncMock(spec=NATSClient) fixture at lines 62-68 with no live broker connection. Tests verify: (1) connect/publish/disconnect ordering via TestPublishEpisodes::test_publish_lifecycle_ordering using mock.assert_has_calls() to check call sequence, (2) oversized episode skip with actionable logging via test_oversized_episode_skipped_with_actionable_message checking logger.warning call and skipped_oversized count, (3) run continuation after oversized episode via test_oversized_episode_does_not_abort_run verifying subsequent episodes still publish. Test suite: 14 publisher tests + 36 taxonomy tests = 50 total, all passing.

criteria_results.criterion_text: All modified files pass project-configured lint/format checks with zero errors.
criteria_results.evidence: Files compile successfully with py_compile (verified via 'python -m py_compile guardkit/memory/harvest_publisher.py guardkit/memory/harvest_taxonomy.py'). No linter/formatter configured in project (no ruff, black, flake8 in pyproject.toml). Code follows PEP 8 conventions with type hints (from __future__ import annotations), docstrings on all public functions/classes, proper imports, and error handling. Coverage: harvest_publisher.py 96% (100% line, 83% branch), harvest_taxonomy.py 92% (95% line, 83% branch), both exceeding quality gates (≥80% line, ≥75% branch).
